research_question: In one disposable Kubernetes application, do DCJI and FullRefresh preserve their modeled gate decisions and UID-conditioned first-effect outcomes while differing in physical acquisition cost? What limits arise after an accepting gate?
scope: One host, one non-production kind cluster, six independent evidence ConfigMaps, a separate scope ConfigMap, an application-policy ConfigMap, a mutation epoch ConfigMap, and one Running-and-Ready target Pod.
extra_authorization_post: One SelfSubjectAccessReview POST per guard, logged separately from GETs; app-policy ConfigMap is not Kubernetes RBAC.
coherence_semantics: Harness-controlled even/odd epoch fence only. No atomic Kubernetes cross-object snapshot and no guarantee against external writers.
model_goal_semantics: Asymmetric attack-capability model: invalidates a,c,e, UID binding or singleton scope. Symmetric b,d,f changes are out-of-model stress.
actuation: Delete exactly one bound Pod using DeleteOptions.preconditions.uid, read back absence or replacement UID. No bulk selector action or complete remediation claim.
primary_safety_endpoints: use-time invalid action after post-gate transition
confirmatory_sample_size_basis: To be frozen after separate calibration using declared precision; no number selected from confirmatory data.
independent_E38_oracle_review: NOT YET SIGNED. Two previous reviews of the historical 29 cards do not by themselves validate the new E38 scenarios.
real_RBAC_permission_revocation_study: NOT IMPLEMENTED; only application policy ConfigMap revocation is included.
host_population_replication: NOT INCLUDED; additional independent physical VMs require a separate signed host-stratified protocol.
high_impact_interpretation: Preserve observed negative results, especially evidence/scope changes after gate. No universal post-gate atomicity claim.
status: NO KUBERNETES EXPERIMENTS EXECUTED IN THIS PACKAGE
